name: party-state
symbols_from_why: Runs against the PINNED BASE ROM: every symbol it reads is vanilla.
description: Slice 1's real deliverable: assert actual GAMEPLAY state, not boot progression. Resumes the committed emerald_party.ss1 save state (player standing in Birch's lab with a level-5 Torchic) and asserts the lead Pokemon's UNENCRYPTED party fields -- level and current HP, which live at fixed offsets in the 100-byte struct Pokemon and are deliberately OUTSIDE the encrypted substructures -- plus a saveblock pointer-chase that re-reads gSaveBlock1Ptr/gSaveBlock2Ptr on every single sample per doc 44's ASLR correction. Counterfactuals: --no-savestate (cold boot; every address stays correct and only memory CONTENT changes) and --counterfactual (every probe base shifted +0x800).

probes.why: gMain.vblankCounter1. Liveness AFTER a state load: proves the resumed emulator is really running the engine's main loop, not frozen on a restored framebuffer. This is the one probe here that is not a gameplay claim.
gMain.callback2 resolved by name. The state resumes INTO the field engine, so this must be CB2_Overworld -- not any of the boot callbacks a cold boot would show.
gPlayerPartyCount. The player owns exactly one Pokemon: the starter handed over by the ROM's own ChooseStarter special in response to button presses. Nothing was written into RAM by the harness.

gPlayerParty[0].level, offset 0x54 in the 100-byte struct Pokemon (box[0x50] + status u32 -> level). THE DOC-34 TARGET: level sits outside the encrypted 48-byte secure block, so it can be asserted without decrypting anything and without knowing the substructure order. Torchic is handed over at level 5.
gPlayerParty[0].hp, offset 0x56 -- current HP, the other doc-34 target and likewise unencrypted. The starter won its scripted first battle and was healed by the post-battle script, so it is at full.

gPlayerParty[0].maxHP, offset 0x58. Asserted only as a relation to hp and as a sane range: maxHP is DERIVED FROM IVs, which are re-rolled on every cold boot, so an exact value is a property of this committed state and not of the engine. It is the boundary between 'assert the number' and 'assert the invariant', and it belongs on the invariant side.

gPlayerParty[0].personality, offset 0x00, unencrypted. Exact-valued on purpose: it identifies THIS committed save state. If someone regenerates the state, this assertion fails loudly instead of the spec quietly asserting a different Pokemon.

gPlayerParty[0].otId, offset 0x04, unencrypted. Cross-checked below against SaveBlock2.playerTrainerId reached by a completely different path (a pointer chase through IWRAM). Two structures agreeing on one number is much harder to produce by accident than either number alone.
gSaveBlock1Ptr read as a pointer and resolved back to a symbol name. Doc 44: never cache this.

THE SAVEBLOCK DEREF PROBE. *gSaveBlock1Ptr + 0x04 = SaveBlock1.location.mapGroup (struct WarpData: s8 mapGroup, s8 mapNum, s8 warpId, s16 x, s16 y). The pointer is re-read on EVERY sample. Map group 1 = the indoor-maps group; see mapnum.

*gSaveBlock1Ptr + 0x05 = SaveBlock1.location.mapNum. 1.4 is Birch's lab -- the map the engine warps you into ONLY after winning the scripted first battle. Asserting the map is asserting that a real scripted sequence ran.

*gSaveBlock2Ptr + 0x00 = SaveBlock2.playerName[8], as raw bytes. A cold boot leaves this all-zero (observed in boot-progression); a real save has charmap bytes terminated by EOS (0xFF). Asserted as 'first byte is neither 0x00 nor 0xFF', i.e. the player has a name -- not as an exact string, because which letter the naming screen's tap landed on was never chosen deliberately.
The same byte as a number, so it can be compared. Split out because 'bytes' probes carry hex strings, not integers.

*gSaveBlock2Ptr + 0x0A = SaveBlock2.playerTrainerId[4]. Read as bytes because the field is a u8[4] at an odd offset -- a u32 read there would be unaligned and the hardware would rotate it. Compared against the starter's otId, reached through gPlayerParty in EWRAM by a completely different route.
gSaveBlock2Ptr itself, for the resolve-back-to-a-name check. Doc 44 again: re-read, never cached.

gBattleOutcome -- half of the battle pair doc 34 §8 named for this slice. The state was captured just after the scripted Birch-rescue battle, so this is the RETAINED outcome of a battle that really ran, not a live one. That is the point: the engine still carries the result, so a battle can be asserted without a battle save state.

gBattleTypeFlags -- the other half. Reads 0x14 = BATTLE_TYPE_IS_MASTER (1<<2) | BATTLE_TYPE_FIRST_BATTLE (1<<4), with BATTLE_TYPE_TRAINER (1<<3) CLEAR, which is exactly right: the Birch rescue is a scripted WILD battle, not a trainer battle. Constants from include/constants/battle.h:48-52 at the pin.

assert.why: The resumed emulator is executing, not frozen.
Resumed into the field engine on every sample. A cold boot is in MainCB2_Intro here, so this is one of the assertions --no-savestate must break.
Exactly one Pokemon owned.
DOC-34 TARGET 1: the lead's level, read unencrypted at offset 0x54.
and it does not drift while the game idles.
DOC-34 TARGET 2: the lead's CURRENT HP, unencrypted at offset 0x56.
Standing still costs no HP -- the invariant half of the HP claim, which holds for any state, not just this one.
maxHP is IV-derived and re-rolled per cold boot, so it gets a range, not an exact number. A level-5 Torchic cannot be outside this.
hp (20) <= maxHP: the mon is not over-healed. Written as a constant because the harness has no cross-probe comparison; the number comes from the hp assertion above.
This is THE committed Torchic. Regenerating the save state changes this, and the spec should say so out loud rather than silently asserting a different Pokemon.
The starter's original-trainer ID.
The re-read SaveBlock1 pointer resolves into gSaveblock1's storage.
THE SAVEBLOCK DEREF ASSERTION, half 1: map group 1.
half 2: map 1.4, Birch's lab -- reachable only by winning the scripted first battle.
Every pointer chase landed on readable memory.
The re-read SaveBlock2 pointer resolves into gSaveblock2's storage.

The player has a name. Zero is what a cold boot shows here, so this discriminates against --no-savestate; it does NOT discriminate against --counterfactual (garbage is usually nonzero), which is exactly why this spec carries both counterfactuals.
...and the name is not the empty string (EOS at index 0).

SaveBlock2.playerTrainerId == the starter's otId (0x86df9fa6, little-endian), reached through a pointer chase in IWRAM while otId was read directly out of EWRAM. Two structures agreeing on one 32-bit number.
The SaveBlock2 chase landed on readable memory on every sample.
The name does not change while the game idles -- proof the chase is reading a stable field rather than wandering.

B_OUTCOME_WON (include/constants/battle.h:94). The scripted first battle was fought and WON. Until this assertion, the win was only inferred from the post-battle map warp; now it is read out of the engine's own outcome byte.

0x14 = IS_MASTER | FIRST_BATTLE, TRAINER clear. Asserted as an exact word rather than a bit test because the harness has no bitmask op -- and because the bit that is ABSENT (TRAINER) is as load-bearing as the ones present: it says the battle asserted above was the wild Birch-rescue battle and not some other.
